name: Soil-hauling e-manifest and GPS compliance and dispatch tool for small hauling firms and civil contractors
buyer: Small trucking firms, civil contractors and soil-yard operators carrying construction soil (about 6,000 trucks a day needed; 5,303 GPS applications by Jan 2026)
trigger: NLMA full-flow soil regime from 1 Jan 2026: every trip needs an e-manifest at each entry and exit point, plus GPS approved under MOI's 18 July 2025 vehicle tracking spec; small trucks now allowed; Waste Disposal Act amendment pending to add national flow reporting and penalties
existing: State e-manifest app plus soilmove system (free). GPS box vendors sell hardware (one lists NT$380 for a unit said to meet both NLMA and MOENV specs). Taichung has its own city app. Competitor search found no SaaS that links dispatch, manifests and cost or disposal-fee books.
unchecked: Whether the state app already covers dispatch and ledgers; whether there is an API or data export; hauler count and willingness to pay; how pending Waste Disposal Act changes will affect it; whether the GPS vendors bundle fleet software.

first_check.duty: Real and in force. Since 1 Jan 2026 the NLMA's (國土管理署) nationwide full-flow regime for construction surplus soil (營建剩餘土石方) applies. Every trip from site to receiving yard needs an electronic manifest (電子聯單) showing the project, route, soil type and volume, and every truck must carry a GPS unit that has passed NLMA type approval. The type-approval procedure is published on nlma.gov.tw. The NLMA gave a GPS transition buffer to the end of February 2026 and opened GPS applications to small trucks. The frequency is every trip. Penalties are not uniform yet: enforcement currently runs through the administrative scheme and local rules, and I did not find a specific national fine. The draft Waste Disposal Act Article 10-1 (MOENV notice of 29 May 2025) would make online reporting and GPS mandatory and let MOI set national rules and penalties. UDN reported on 18 May 2026 that the bill was only in Legislative Yuan committee review. One summary mentions a third reading, but I could not date it or confirm that the soil clause survived. Treat the amendment as pending or unverified.
first_check.market: About 15,000 gravel and soil trucks nationwide (UDN and CTEE, Jan-Feb 2026). One undated report gives 6,743 NLMA GPS applications, of which 6,223 were cleared to operate, plus 1,649 MOENV-equipped trucks. There are about 140 soil storage and processing yards (土資場), but only 18 operating sites with fill capacity (Dec 2025). I found no register count of hauling firms; a guess of a few thousand mostly small owner-operator firms is unverified.
first_check.competitor: The core reporting job is already covered for free by the state soilmove e-manifest system and app, and some cities run their own (Taichung's app, Tainan's QR-code checks at yards). NLMA-approved GPS vendors sell boxes bundled with their own fleet platforms, offering live tracking and trip history. One vendor (a LINE official page) claims a single unit meets both NLMA and MOENV specs. Neither the state system nor the GPS vendors appear to link dispatch, manifests and cost or disposal-fee ledgers in a SaaS for small haulers, but I did not reach that conclusion exhaustively. Foreign analogues exist (SoilFLO, Soil Connect eRegulatory) but they are not localized for Taiwan. I could not confirm whether the state system offers an API or data export, so integration risk is high.
first_check.reason: The duty is real, applies to every trip, and caused a national crisis in early 2026 (the "土方之亂"). But the state e-manifest system is free, and GPS vendors already bundle fleet tracking, so the remaining gap is only the dispatch and ledger layer that ties manifests to fees and costs. Small haulers are fragmented owner-operators who are not very digital and are price-sensitive (GPS units sell for around NT$380). Whether the state system has an API is unknown, which makes the MVP risky. The pending Waste Disposal Act changes may alter the rules again. GPS vendors and industry associations are the natural channels, but those vendors could add this feature themselves. The opportunity is moderate to low for a solo founder.

challenge_check.killer: No single killer was found. The weaknesses: the free state soilmove e-manifest app, plus city systems such as Taichung's GPS app built by 天眼衛星, cover the filing itself. Approved GPS vendors (e.g. page.line.me/mhb6106n) bundle fleet platforms with reports. I found no public API or data export for integration (unverified). Not reached: whether the June 2026 Waste Disposal Act text adds a separate reporting duty.
challenge_check.reason: I found nothing that kills it. The regime started on 1 Jan 2026 and has not been deferred. An April 2026 report says the GPS and e-reporting mandate still applies, and it is being extended to temporary storage sites. The Waste Disposal Act amendment reportedly passed third reading in June 2026; I did not confirm the final soil-flow wording. My searches found no Taiwanese SaaS that links dispatch, e-manifests and trip or fee billing. But the free state soilmove app and city systems (Taichung's is built by 天眼衛星) already do the mandatory filing. Approved GPS vendors bundle fleet platforms with trip reports. There is no public API spec, and the market is about 15,000 trucks, so the add-on value is a thin convenience. I keep the score at 4.
